Support · Saving locations

Photos location and EXIF GPS are related—but not the same.

LensPin saves an approved point to the location associated with the item in Apple Photos. It does not write GPS into the image file's EXIF metadata or modify the original photo or RAW file.

Reviewed October 8, 2026

Apple Photos library location

This is the location Apple Photos associates with the asset. It powers the Info map and location-based browsing. LensPin adds this location only after you confirm the selection.

What LensPin does not change

LensPin does not edit image-file EXIF GPS, create a rendered replacement, modify the original photo or RAW file, or create an XMP sidecar. EXIF camera, capture-time, and original-GPS fields may be read as matching evidence, but they remain unchanged.

Exports can vary.

Whether Apple Photos includes its library location in a shared or exported derivative depends on the export path and Photos settings. LensPin makes no file-level GPS change, so verify a sample if embedded metadata is required elsewhere.

Writeback outcome

Each item is reported as Added, Failed, or Skipped based on the Apple Photos library-location update. There is no secondary EXIF editing step or EXIF fallback in the current version.

Why a photo is skipped

LensPin reads the Photos item immediately before writing. If another app, device, or sync operation added a location after the preview was created, LensPin skips that photo rather than overwriting it.

Completion statuses

✓

Added

The Photos-library location was successfully written.

×

Failed

The location write did not complete. Keep the displayed per-item reason for support.

↷

Skipped

The item was intentionally left alone, commonly because it already had a location.

LensPin album

Only photos whose location was actually added are collected in the LensPin album. If album collection fails, the completion screen shows a separate warning; it does not undo or hide a successful location write.

How to verify

  1. Open the LensPin album after the batch.
  2. Open a photo in Apple Photos and inspect the Info map and coordinates.
  3. Compare the point with the route and surrounding photos.
  4. If embedded file GPS is required elsewhere, inspect an exported sample separately; LensPin does not provide that file-level writeback.
